A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EgoBrain dataset and Brain-TIM framework. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including matching content moved between sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original cross-subject and cross-scene classification experiments, component ablations and prediction analyses in Tables 1–2 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds baseline results, a spatial-fusion comparison and action-level confusion matrices in its appendices.

M1.justification: Brain-TIM retains its frozen VideoMAE/LaBraM encoders, temporal and modality embeddings, Transformer and weighted modality losses. The feature-extraction material is relocated, and the verb/action-head description is expanded without establishing an actual model revision. Spatial fusion is introduced as a comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 61-hour, 40-participant EgoBrain dataset, 29 actions, 10 verbs and two generalization scenarios. Play I–III and the participant/action visualizations already exist in v2. The revised object-arrangement description does not establish new collected data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 retains the unimodal comparisons and adds uniform chance, class-prior random and majority-class baselines in Table 4, plus a spatial-fusion comparator in Table 5. These extend comparisons within the existing benchmark.

E3.justification: v2 Section 3 describes the held-out scene as having a similar object arrangement; v3 Appendix B.3 specifies a completely different arrangement. This is a reported setting revision, without evidence of recollection or rerunning. Appendix E also introduces a fusion control with fewer, wider tokens. Existing split sizes, metrics and backbone configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds an ablation testing temporal versus spatial fusion. Appendix F adds fine-grained error analysis through 29-action confusion matrices, while Figure 4 exposes previously omitted cross-group verb errors. Existing component ablations and cases remain. Appendix D's robustness discussion interprets retained results rather than reporting a new robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions report experimental means and standard deviations across five random seeds. v3 applies the same practice to the added fusion comparison; it introduces no new run-count policy, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: The main benchmark and component-ablation values are unchanged. v3 adds baseline rates, including 7.02% majority-class action accuracy, and spatial-fusion results of 83.74±0.62% verb and 64.81±1.04% action accuracy, alongside retained Brain-TIM scores of 83.43±0.41% and 66.70±0.83%. Full confusion entries are added, and Figure 5a corrects the swapped drinking-example predictions.

T1.justification: Appendix E newly defines the spatial-fusion sequence mathematically, including its (N+Q)×3D shape. Existing Brain-TIM task definitions, temporal embeddings and loss equations are retained or relocated. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain the synchronized EEG–egocentric dataset, Brain-TIM benchmark and evidence of modality complementarity. The abstract retains the same dataset scale and 66.70% action accuracy. Expanded motivation and supporting experiments do not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking overlapping windows to tolerance of synchronization jitter, EEG performance to environmental invariance and additional training subjects, and temporal fusion to finer action discrimination. It also explains the taxonomy and supervision choices. These extend interpretation; the environmental-invariance explanation is not supported by a new controlled experiment.

D1.justification: v3 supplies explicit Hugging Face dataset and GitHub code access pointers, replacing v2's general sharing statement. It newly documents validation-based checkpoint selection and verb/action supervision, but omits v2's explicit reference-display synchronization statement. Most acquisition, preprocessing and encoder details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds a substantive comparison with ToMCAT and citations concerning action recognition, hand-pose estimation and spatial reasoning. It also acknowledges audio, IMU, gaze and other modalities in existing egocentric datasets instead of broadly calling them vision-only, while retaining its positioning around synchronized EEG.

P1.justification: The existing exposition is substantially reorganized: feature extraction moves from Appendix A into Section 4.3, detailed temporal embeddings move into Appendix C, and participant, split and duration descriptions are consolidated in Appendix B. The introduction and dataset narrative are expanded, with revised headings, cross-references and publication information.

P2.justification: Figure 4 replaces four grouped 5×5 plots with two full 10×10 matrices. v3 adds full action-confusion figures and tables for activity categories, reference baselines, fusion comparisons and abbreviations. Figure 5's prediction labels are corrected. Most setup, architecture and dataset-example imagery is retained.

improvement.justification: The added reference baselines and fusion comparison address gaps in contextualizing performance, while fuller error visualizations, clearer method organization and concrete access pointers improve scrutiny and reproducibility. These benefits are limited by untested causal explanations. v3 also introduces a case-study inconsistency: Section 5.3 says the PowerPoint example is predicted as Draw Pictures, while Figure 5b still shows operate paint. Overall, the additions provide a modest quality gain.
